To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the cultural characteristics of the Egyptian society are the main barrier to the successful adoption of KM and innovation; and, 2) the lack of trust between employees is the major barrier to the adoption of KM and Innovation.
the success of KM, innovation and competitive advantage can be moderated and even be compromised by organizational and national cultural characteristics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
knowledge transfer and knowledge accumulation in organizations.
how the cultural context in which knowledge management and knowledge transfer take place can impact on the innovation process and the achievement of competitive differentiation.
the relationship between culture and knowledge management, and the role of culture in knowledge management and knowledge transfer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
knowledge management is an essential component of the innovation process, and that it is a critical component of the innovation management process.
knowledge management, knowledge transfer, innovation and competitive advantage can be moderated by cultural factors in the Middle East and North Africa region.

the cultural issues identified by Hofstede (1980, 1991, 2001) do impact on the knowledge management processes and the innovation process, and that these cultural variables may be moderated by national and organizational cultural variables, which are also impacted by the national cultural variables.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
knowledge management is a key factor in the development of competitive advantage and that this is a function of the ability to innovate.
knowledge management, innovation, and competitive advantage are all interrelated and interdependent.
we have developed a framework for understanding the role of knowledge management in innovation, which is a critical success factor in today's competitive global environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
knowledge management, innovation, and competitive advantage can be moderated and even hampered by cultural considerations.
the knowledge accumulation process can be affected by national cultural characteristics, and that the knowledge transfer process is affected by organizational culture.
